children: Metal stocks ended lower on Monday, with Adani Enterprises, National Aluminium Co (Nalco), Hindustan Zinc and other shares declining, tracking weakness in bullion prices after US Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh indicated the possibility of an interest rate hike.
The Nifty Metal index fell 2.45 per cent, with 13 of its 15 constituents trading lower.
Silver futures for October delivery fell nearly 1 per cent to USD 66.86 per ounce on the COMEX.
Hindustan Zinc, a major silver producer, fell over 4 per cent, while its parent company Vedanta declined more than 3 per cent.
Major aluminium producers Hindalco Industries and National Aluminium Co fell nearly 4 per cent and over 2 per cent, respectively.
September aluminium futures were flat at Rs 345.7 per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange.
"Base metals prices are under pressure as Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh came his closest yet to acknowledging interest rate hikes may lie ahead," SMC said in a report.

On Friday, Warsh said, "We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do. That's our job, our mandate and our charge to keep."

The possibility of higher US interest rates weighed on bullion and base metal prices. A rate hike can also put pressure on metal shares as lower commodity prices can affect the earnings outlook of metal producers. This, in turn, can weigh on their stocks in India.

title: Nifty Metal down 2.5%; Adani Enterprises, Nalco, Hind Zinc decline up to 10%: Here's why
